title: Jacobi matrix of primes
plain: Build an infinite tridiagonal (Jacobi) matrix with zero diagonal and the primes 2, 3, 5, 7, ... on the off-diagonals. The standard criteria for purely absolutely continuous spectrum need the off-diagonal sequence to vary regularly, and they just fail because prime gaps fluctuate. Decide whether the spectrum is nevertheless purely absolutely continuous on the whole real line.
math: Let $J$ be the self-adjoint Jacobi operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb N)$ given by $(Ju)_n=p_{n-1}u_{n-1}+p_nu_{n+1}$ (with $p_0u_0:=0$), where $p_n$ is the $n$-th prime. It is self-adjoint by Carleman's criterion, since $\sum1/p_n=\infty$. Decide whether $\sigma(J)=\sigma_{ac}(J)=\mathbb R$ with no singular part.
